title: Zero Day
synopsis: A cyberattack takes the country down for one minute and kills three thousand people. You're a former president, asked back to chair the investigation. The answer, you suspect, is in your old administration's closets.

nodes.text: FBI Director, on a sofa in your study. The brief is one minute long. The minute was, as far as anyone can prove, foreign. Your Wife will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Take the commission” than after “Refuse and recommend someone.”

choices.consequence: You commit to take the commission. It carries you into Your Wife while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
You refuse and recommend someone. The way toward Your Wife opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: She does not want you to take it. She is, in the marital sense, correct. You take it anyway. She, in the marital sense, supports you. Both choices lead to Staff, but “Promise her a date” arrives there with a different cost than “Promise her honesty.”

choices.consequence: You choose to promise her a date. By Staff, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.
You commit to promise her honesty. It carries you into Staff while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: You build a small staff — a former general counsel, a young technologist, a press secretary you respect. First Hearing comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Lead with the lawyer” and “Lead with the technologist.”

choices.consequence: You choose to lead with the lawyer. By First Hearing, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.
You choose to lead with the technologist. By First Hearing, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: The first hearing is, as expected, theater. You permit a small amount of it. You cannot avoid The Whistle; you can only decide whether “Use the theater” or “Cut to substance” defines the person who reaches it.

choices.consequence: You use the theater. The way toward The Whistle opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.
You commit to cut to substance. It carries you into The Whistle while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: An NSA analyst comes to you quietly. He has data the agency has, he believes, redacted dishonestly. You verify him. Memory Issues is already waiting. What changes is whether “Receive the data” or “Recommend formal whistleblower channels first” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You receive the data. The way toward Memory Issues opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.
You commit to recommend formal whistleblower channels first. It carries you into Memory Issues while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: You notice, between meetings, that you are forgetting things. Names. Dates. The press secretary does not, you can tell, want to be the one who tells you. Both choices lead to The Daughter, but “See a doctor immediately” arrives there with a different cost than “Hide it for now.”

choices.consequence: You commit to see a doctor immediately. It carries you into The Daughter while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
You choose to hide it for now. By The Daughter, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Your daughter, a congresswoman, has been briefed by her own staff that you are missing things. She comes to you. The conversation is difficult and loving. Closet, Old Administration is already waiting. What changes is whether “Tell her everything” or “Tell her you'll handle it” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You tell her everything. The way toward Closet, Old Administration opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.
You choose to tell her you'll handle it. By Closet, Old Administration, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: The whistleblower's data points to a backdoor you signed off on during your presidency. You did not, at the time, understand it fully. You sign off on many things. Press Secretary is already waiting. What changes is whether “Take responsibility publicly” or “Address it quietly first” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You commit to take responsibility publicly. It carries you into Press Secretary while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
You commit to address it quietly first. It carries you into Press Secretary while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Your press secretary asks if you want a statement. He has, separately, written two drafts. One is a full apology. One is a careful one. Director comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Use the full apology” and “Use the careful one.”

choices.consequence: You commit to use the full apology. It carries you into Director while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
You commit to use the careful one. It carries you into Director while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: The current FBI Director meets you off the record. He is loyal to the institution. He is, in this case, on your side. Asia Trip comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Coordinate with him” and “Stay separate.”

choices.consequence: You commit to coordinate with him. It carries you into Asia Trip while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
You stay separate. The way toward Asia Trip opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: A trip to Tokyo, Seoul, and Taipei, with the question 'who did this.' The answer, in your gut, is not what the briefings say. Memory Test is already waiting. What changes is whether “Trust your gut” or “Trust the briefings” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You trust your gut. The way toward Memory Test opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.
You choose to trust the briefings. By Memory Test, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Your doctor confirms early cognitive issues. The press will, eventually, learn. You decide what shape the disclosure takes. The road still runs toward Your Old Chief of Staff. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Disclose now” and choosing “Disclose at the end of the commission.”

choices.consequence: You choose to disclose now. By Your Old Chief of Staff, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Disclose at the end of the commission
choices.consequence: You commit to disclose at the end of the commission. It carries you into Your Old Chief of Staff while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Your old chief of staff is, you discover, lobbying for the cybersecurity firm at the center of the closet you just opened. He is a friend. You cannot avoid The Quiet Threat; you can only decide whether “Confront him” or “Subpoena him” defines the person who reaches it.

choices.consequence: You choose to confront him. By The Quiet Threat, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.
You subpoena him. The way toward The Quiet Threat opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Someone in the executive branch — quietly, formally — would prefer you didn't. You cannot avoid Your Wife, Again; you can only decide whether “Push back through formal channels” or “Push back publicly” defines the person who reaches it.

choices.consequence: You choose to push back through formal channels. By Your Wife, Again, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.
You choose to push back publicly. By Your Wife, Again, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: She makes coffee in the morning and doesn't ask. You realize, gratefully, that being silent with someone is also a form of supporting them. Hearing, Final Day will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Tell her everything” than after “Just thank her.”

choices.consequence: You choose to tell her everything. By Hearing, Final Day, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.
You just thank her. The way toward Hearing, Final Day opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Final hearing. The room is, somehow, both packed and tired. You speak for fourteen minutes without notes. You realize, mid-sentence, that you are, almost, telling the truth. Both choices lead to The Report, but “Tell all of it” arrives there with a different cost than “Tell most of it.”

choices.consequence: You commit to tell all of it. It carries you into The Report while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
You choose to tell most of it. By The Report, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: The final report is honest. It also, at your insistence, names the backdoor you signed. The press, expecting cover-up, doesn't quite know what to do. The road still runs toward Resignation. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Take questions immediately” and choosing “Let the report speak.”

choices.consequence: You choose to take questions immediately. By Resignation, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.
You let the report speak. The way toward Resignation opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: You resign from a board you sit on. The resignation is, in a quiet way, the punishment that fits. You cannot avoid Daughter, Calling; you can only decide whether “Resign quietly” or “Resign with a public statement” defines the person who reaches it.

choices.consequence: You resign quietly. The way toward Daughter, Calling opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.
You resign with a public statement. The way toward Daughter, Calling opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Your daughter calls. She read the report. She tells you she is proud of you. You realize, in your seventies, that this matters more to you than any other call you have taken. You cannot avoid Memoir; you can only decide whether “Tell her what's been going on with the doctor” or “Save it for dinner” defines the person who reaches it.

choices.text: Tell her what's been going on with the doctor
choices.consequence: You tell her what's been going on with the doctor. The way toward Memoir opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.
You save it for dinner. The way toward Memoir opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: You decide to write a memoir. The memoir is, finally, the honest one. The publisher, surprising you, is grateful. Both choices lead to Last Year, but “Lead with the failure” arrives there with a different cost than “Lead with the lessons.”

choices.consequence: You lead with the failure. The way toward Last Year opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.
You commit to lead with the lessons. It carries you into Last Year while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: The diagnosis progresses, slowly. You spend time at the lake with your wife. The country, mostly, recovers. The paths divide here: “Spend the last good year with family” leads into Legacy of the Report, while “Spend it on one last public good” makes Lake House the next reckoning. A third choice, “Take the third path,” keeps One Last Good in play.

choices.text: Spend the last good year with family
choices.consequence: You choose to spend the last good year with family. By Legacy of the Report, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Spend it on one last public good
choices.consequence: You choose to spend it on one last public good. By Lake House, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.
Some endings reveal themselves last. You commit to take the third path. It carries you into One Last Good while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: The report becomes the foundation for the cybersecurity reforms that follow. You are remembered for the honesty more than the presidency. You decide, late, that that is exactly right. The road into Legacy of the Report began with “Spend the last good year with family” in Last Year; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.
You spend your last good years at the lake with your wife and daughter and three grandchildren who think you are mostly fun. The country goes on. You let it. You let yourself go on too.

You spend your last year on a quiet, careful piece of policy work. You finish it. The next administration adopts it. You don't, in the end, see it implemented. But the country is, by a small measure, safer because of you.
